5.title: Collateral Performance: Delinquencies, Net Loss and Severity
5.shortTitle: Read the health of the loan pool

sections.label: Signals
sections.title: Track the signals before losses arrive
sections.kicker: DASHBOARD MODE: late payments are an early warning system.
sections.lead: Monthly reporting follows loans from delinquency through charge-off and recovery so stress is visible before it reaches the bonds.

bullets.title: Delinquencies
bullets.text: Measure loans 30, 60 and 90+ days late by balance or count; older buckets are closer to charge-off.

bullets.title: Charge-offs
bullets.text: Gross charge-offs are principal balances declared uncollectible during the period.

bullets.title: Recoveries
bullets.text: Auction proceeds and later collections reduce the economic loss after charge-off.

bullets.title: Prepayments
bullets.text: Early principal repayments shorten weighted-average life and change remaining cash flows.

sections.callout: Watch the direction of 60+ and 90+, not only the latest headline number.

sections.label: Math
sections.title: Turn servicing data into comparable ratios
sections.kicker: STAT CHECK: use the right numerator and denominator.
sections.lead: Delinquency percentages divide late-payment balances by current collateral; net loss and severity connect defaults to recoveries.

bullets.title: 30+ delinquency
bullets.text: Add 30–59, 60–89 and 90+ balances, then divide by current collateral.

bullets.title: 60+ delinquency
bullets.text: Add 60–89 and 90+ balances, then divide by current collateral.

bullets.title: Net loss
bullets.text: Net loss equals gross charge-offs minus recoveries.

bullets.title: Severity
bullets.text: A same-period approximation is net loss divided by gross charge-offs.

sections.callout: Lower recoveries raise severity even when gross charge-offs do not change.

sections.label: CNL curve
sections.title: Read losses as a path, not a single month
sections.kicker: TREND LINE: compare actual performance with the expected path.
sections.lead: Cumulative net loss adds net losses since closing and expresses them against the original pool, creating a curve comparable across seasoning and vintages.

bullets.title: CNL percentage
bullets.text: Cumulative net losses divided by original pool balance shows how much starting collateral has been lost.

bullets.title: Static pool
bullets.text: A vintage view follows one origination cohort by months on book.

bullets.title: Trust view
bullets.text: A securitized-pool view includes amortization and prepayments.

bullets.title: Seasoning
bullets.text: Auto losses often emerge earlier and taper as the pool seasons and borrower equity grows.

sections.callout: Ratings analysis asks whether enhancement survives a stressed CNL path, not just today's loss rate.

sections.label: Performance lab
sections.title: Diagnose a weakening pool and call the cash action
sections.kicker: ANALYST ROUND: calculate the ratios, then predict the waterfall.
sections.lead: Use the source exercise to turn raw collateral data into a performance diagnosis and a next-payment-date decision.

bullets.title: Delinquency inputs
bullets.text: On an $88.0mm current pool, use $1.2mm at 30 days, $0.6mm at 60 days and $0.4mm at 90+ to calculate 30+, 60+ and 90+.

bullets.title: Loss inputs
bullets.text: $500k charge-offs less $275k recoveries gives $225k net loss and 45% severity.

bullets.title: Recovery shock
bullets.text: If recoveries fall to $200k with charge-offs unchanged, net loss rises to $300k and severity to 60%.

bullets.title: Trigger decision
bullets.text: At 1.085x OC against a 1.10x threshold, predict zero equity, trapped spread and sequential senior pay.

sections.callout: The lab links collateral deterioration → higher loss → weaker protection → cash trapping.

flashcards.back: The 60–89 and 90+ balances divided by current collateral.
Gross charge-offs minus recoveries.
Loss after recoveries as a share of charged-off or defaulted principal.
Net losses since closing, commonly divided by original pool balance.
The share moving from one delinquency stage to the next.

quiz.q: Which bucket is generally closest to near-term charge-off?
quiz.explain: 90+ is furthest through the missed-payment sequence.

quiz.q: Charge-offs are $500k and recoveries $275k. Net loss?
quiz.explain: $500k minus $275k equals $225k.

quiz.q: What usually happens to severity when used-car prices weaken?
quiz.explain: Lower auction proceeds leave more loss after recovery.

quiz.q: What denominator commonly defines trust CNL%?
quiz.explain: Trust CNL is commonly divided by original pool balance.

quiz.q: Typical response to a CNL trigger breach?
quiz.explain: The structure protects seniors and pauses residual cash.

6.title: Hands-on: Build a Mini Waterfall
6.prerequisite: Days 4–5 · Waterfalls, triggers and collateral performance

sections.label: Inputs
sections.title: Set up one payment period
sections.kicker: MODEL START: balances in, collections in, assumptions visible.
sections.lead: A small waterfall begins with collections, fees, note balances and coupons, plus reserve and OC rails.

bullets.title: Collections
bullets.text: Enter asset interest, asset principal and recoveries.

bullets.title: Liabilities
bullets.text: Enter Class A and B beginning balances and annual coupons.

bullets.title: Expenses
bullets.text: Include servicing, trustee or administration fees and swap cost.

bullets.title: Protection
bullets.text: Carry reserve beginning and target plus beginning and target OC.

sections.callout: Document every shortcut in Notes so the logic remains reviewable.

sections.label: Interest
sections.title: Pay operating costs and note interest first
sections.kicker: CASH QUEUE: calculate obligations before principal and equity.
sections.lead: Use monthly fractions of annual rates to calculate servicing and note interest before measuring excess spread.

bullets.title: Servicer fee
bullets.text: Approximate beginning collateral × annual servicing rate ÷ 12.

bullets.title: Class A interest
bullets.text: $7.0mm at 5% costs about $29,167 monthly.

bullets.title: Class B interest
bullets.text: $2.0mm at 8% costs about $13,333 monthly.

bullets.title: Excess spread
bullets.text: Asset interest plus recoveries less servicing, trustee, swap and note interest.

sections.callout: The sample produces about $51,167 of excess spread before principal.

sections.label: Principal
sections.title: Apply principal sequentially and update protection
sections.kicker: PAYDOWN MODE: senior balance first.
sections.lead: Available principal pays Class A before B, while spread first addresses reserve needs and then follows OC rules.

bullets.title: Sequential pay
bullets.text: $300k reduces Class A from $7.0mm to $6.7mm; B stays $2.0mm.

bullets.title: Reserve top-up
bullets.text: Fund the target gap from positive spread.

bullets.title: OC build
bullets.text: OC grows through trapped spread and notes amortizing faster than assets.

bullets.title: Carry forward
bullets.text: Ending note, reserve and OC balances become next-period beginnings.

sections.callout: Every ending balance must reconcile to the next beginning balance.

sections.label: Trigger
sections.title: Let the OC test decide equity versus trapping
sections.kicker: DECISION GATE: pass pays equity; fail rebuilds the shield.
sections.lead: If adjusted collateral divided by rated notes is below target, equity is zero and spread is retained.

bullets.title: OC ratio
bullets.text: Use the document definition or stated proxy.

bullets.title: Pass
bullets.text: After reserve needs, spread may reach equity.

bullets.title: Fail
bullets.text: Set equity to zero and apply spread to reserve or OC.

bullets.title: Period 2
bullets.text: Carry balances forward and force a fail to observe trap-and-turbo.

sections.callout: At a 1.10x target, 1.085x fails even if the gap looks small.

flashcards.back: Asset interest plus recoveries minus fees, swap costs and note interest.
Principal pays Class A before Class B.
Cash retained to restore the reserve to target.
Adjusted collateral divided by outstanding rated notes.
Stop equity, retain spread and accelerate senior principal during a fail.

quiz.q: Where does spread go when OC is below target?
quiz.explain: A failing test traps cash to rebuild protection.

quiz.q: Who receives principal first sequentially?
quiz.explain: Sequential pay reduces Class A first.

quiz.q: Which item reduces spread before equity?
quiz.explain: Fees and note interest are paid first.

quiz.q: What does trapped spread do?
quiz.explain: It helps OC move toward target.

quiz.q: What happens to ending balances?
quiz.explain: Carry-forward creates a coherent multi-period path.

7.title: Read a Presale and Build a Deal Summary
7.shortTitle: Extract the deal in ten minutes
7.prerequisite: Days 1–6 · Structure, performance and waterfall mechanics

sections.label: Sources
sections.title: Know what each deal document can tell you
sections.kicker: SOURCE CHECK: summary, marketing or definitive rulebook?
sections.lead: A presale explains agency analysis, marketing materials add deal color and legal documents control final terms.

bullets.title: Presale
bullets.text: Use for collateral, ratings, expected loss, stress and CE analysis.

bullets.title: Issuer deck
bullets.text: Use for capital-stack and market narrative, remembering it is marketing.

bullets.title: Term sheet
bullets.text: Use for indicative sizes, coupons, WAL and pay features.

bullets.title: Indenture
bullets.text: Use for exact waterfall and trigger language.

sections.callout: A presale helps navigation; it does not replace definitive documents.

sections.label: Extract
sections.title: Run the ten-minute deal extraction
sections.kicker: SPEED RUN: stack, collateral, protection, rules and servicing.
sections.lead: A disciplined skim captures what determines cash timing, loss protection and investor risk.

bullets.title: Stack and collateral
bullets.text: Capture sizes, ratings, coupons and WALs with credit mix, APR, seasoning, LTV and concentrations.

bullets.title: Enhancement
bullets.text: Record subordination, initial OC, reserve and expected spread.

bullets.title: Rules
bullets.text: Find sequential or pro-rata conditions, step-up, PDL and all key tests.

bullets.title: Operations
bullets.text: Note remittance, lockbox, advances, backup servicing and downgrade rules.

bullets.title: Agency view
bullets.text: Capture base loss, severity and rating stress vectors.

sections.callout: Expose decision-relevant mechanics rather than copying the report.

sections.label: One-pager
sections.title: Compress the transaction into one useful page
sections.kicker: PM VIEW: make the system legible to the next reader.
sections.lead: Connect collateral risk to capital, enhancement, payment logic and controls.

bullets.title: Identity
bullets.text: State issuer, series and pool profile.

bullets.title: Capital
bullets.text: Show classes, ratings, coupons, WAL and closing CE.

bullets.title: Cash
bullets.text: Summarize pay rules, tests, reserve and breach behavior.

bullets.title: Stress
bullets.text: Capture servicing, cash control and rating logic.

sections.callout: A colleague should be able to explain both normal and stress paths.

sections.label: Deal-summary lab
sections.title: Turn a sample presale into a cash-flow decision
sections.kicker: TEN-MINUTE TEST: extract, calculate and flag.
sections.lead: Apply the one-page method to the source's $100mm illustrative transaction and explain how its conditional pro-rata feature behaves.

bullets.title: Capital stack
bullets.text: Class A is $70mm, Class B $20mm and equity $10mm; subordination to A is 30%.

bullets.title: Closing support
bullets.text: Add 10% OC and a 2% reserve to describe headline support before excess spread.

bullets.title: Trigger case
bullets.text: Pro-rata requires OC at least 12% and 60+ below 2%; observed values are 11.5% and 2.5%.

bullets.title: Cash decision
bullets.text: Both conditions fail: flip sequential, trap spread and pause equity.

bullets.title: Risk flag
bullets.text: Name two terms—such as optional advances or long remittance—that could worsen the stress path.

sections.callout: A deal summary is complete only when its terms produce a clear cash-flow conclusion.

flashcards.back: Agency analysis of collateral, structure, CE, expected loss and preliminary ratings.
Protection visible at close: subordination, OC and reserve.
Principal sharing while specified tests pass.
Ledger of principal used for interest, cured before junior principal.
Collections may be trapped if their servicer fails.

quiz.q: Definitive source for waterfall language?
quiz.explain: Trust documents govern the transaction.

quiz.q: Common closing CE component?
quiz.explain: Reserve, subordination and OC are common.

quiz.q: What can flip pro-rata sequential?
quiz.explain: Tests and documented dates control the flip.

quiz.q: Why do optional advances matter?
quiz.explain: Missed interest may not be advanced.

quiz.q: What should a deal summary connect?
options: Collateral, structure, protection, rules and controls
quiz.explain: It should show how risk changes cash outcomes.

8.title: Pricing, Spreads, WAL and Yield
8.prerequisite: Day 7 · Read a presale and summarize a deal

sections.label: Language
sections.title: Speak the market's pricing language
sections.kicker: PRICE SCREEN: par, coupon, yield and spread are different signals.
sections.lead: A bond's price is quoted per 100 of par, while yield reflects both its coupon and the timing and price of its projected cash flows.

bullets.title: Price
bullets.text: A quote of 99.25 means paying 99.25 per 100 of principal.

bullets.title: Coupon
bullets.text: The contractual rate paid on outstanding note balance.

bullets.title: Yield
bullets.text: The internal rate of return at the purchase price and projected cash flows.

bullets.title: Spread
bullets.text: Yield minus a matched Treasury or swap benchmark; floaters often use discount margin.

sections.callout: A higher coupon is not automatically a higher yield because price and timing also matter.

sections.label: WAL
sections.title: Connect principal timing to investor risk
sections.kicker: TIME EXPOSURE: when principal returns changes what investors demand.
sections.lead: Weighted-average life estimates the average time to principal return and helps investors compare extension exposure.

bullets.title: Shorter WAL
bullets.text: Usually means less time exposed and a tighter required spread, all else equal.

bullets.title: Pro-rata
bullets.text: Sharing principal with juniors can slow senior amortization.

bullets.title: Sequential
bullets.text: Directing principal to seniors can shorten their WAL in stress.

bullets.title: Step-up
bullets.text: A scheduled coupon change affects carry but is not itself WAL.

sections.callout: A long pro-rata window can create extension risk even when current performance looks healthy.

sections.label: Approximation
sections.title: Estimate yield and price sensitivity quickly
sections.kicker: BACK-OF-ENVELOPE: useful intuition before the full cash-flow model.
sections.lead: For roughly level cash flows, approximate yield as coupon carry plus annualized pull-to-par; use WAL as a crude duration proxy for price moves.

bullets.title: Yield formula
bullets.text: y ≈ Coupon ÷ Price + (Par − Price) ÷ (WAL × Price).

bullets.title: Spread
bullets.text: Subtract the maturity-matched benchmark yield from estimated note yield.

bullets.title: Price change
bullets.text: ΔP ≈ −WAL × Δy × Price as a rough amortizing-note proxy.

bullets.title: Precision limit
bullets.text: Use projected cash-flow IRR and proper duration for investment decisions.

sections.callout: The shortcut explains direction and scale; it is not a substitute for cash-flow analytics.

sections.label: Pricing lab
sections.title: Price two notes and test a widening
sections.kicker: MARKET ROUND: calculate, benchmark, then explain the difference.
sections.lead: Use the exercise inputs to estimate yields and spreads for an A note and B note, then shock each spread 40 basis points wider.

bullets.title: Class A input
bullets.text: Coupon 5.75%, price 99.60, WAL 2.6 years and 3-year Treasury 4.90%.

bullets.title: Class B input
bullets.text: Coupon 6.75%, price 98.90, WAL 1.9 years and 2-year Treasury 4.70%.

bullets.title: Widening test
bullets.text: Apply ΔP ≈ −WAL × 0.40% × Price to estimate each price decline.

bullets.title: Decision
bullets.text: Identify two structural features—such as more CE or a tighter sequential flip—that justify tighter Class A pricing.

sections.callout: Structure earns tighter pricing when it improves loss protection or reduces extension exposure.

flashcards.back: The amount paid per 100 of bond principal.
The IRR of projected cash flows at the purchase price.
Note yield minus a maturity-matched Treasury yield.
The average time until principal is returned, weighted by principal payments.
The risk principal returns later than expected, increasing time exposed.

quiz.q: What is spread to Treasury?
quiz.explain: Spread measures yield compensation above a benchmark.

quiz.q: Why does WAL matter?
quiz.explain: Later principal generally means more exposure and extension risk.

quiz.q: What typically reduces senior extension risk in stress?
quiz.explain: Sequential pay directs principal to seniors first.

quiz.q: Is higher coupon always higher yield?
options: No; price and cash-flow timing matter
quiz.explain: Yield is an IRR, not simply the coupon.

quiz.q: Which is the rough price-change formula?
quiz.explain: Price and required yield generally move in opposite directions.

9.title: Surveillance: Trustee Reports, KPIs and Trigger Monitoring

sections.label: Report
sections.title: Turn the monthly report into a control panel
sections.kicker: MONTHLY PULSE: collections, balances, protection and tests.
sections.lead: Trustee and servicer reports show how cash arrived, how it was distributed and whether collateral and structural protection remain on plan.

bullets.title: Collections
bullets.text: Capture interest, principal, recoveries and prepayments.

bullets.title: Liabilities
bullets.text: Reconcile beginning and ending class balances, interest and principal paid.

bullets.title: Support
bullets.text: Track OC, reserve and excess spread.

bullets.title: Performance
bullets.text: Record delinquency buckets, CNL, repurchases and realized losses.

bullets.title: Tests
bullets.text: Extract OC, IC, delinquency and CNL thresholds and pass/fail flags.

sections.callout: A useful tracker reconciles cash and explains why each protection metric moved.

sections.label: KPIs
sections.title: Calculate the six surveillance essentials
sections.kicker: KPI CHECK: ratios turn pages of data into decisions.
sections.lead: A compact tracker puts structural and collateral health on the same line for each payment date.

bullets.title: OC ratio
bullets.text: Adjusted collateral divided by outstanding rated notes.

bullets.title: IC ratio
bullets.text: Interest collections divided by senior fees and note interest due.

bullets.title: 60+ delinquency
bullets.text: 60–89 plus 90+ balances divided by current collateral.

bullets.title: CNL percentage
bullets.text: Cumulative net loss divided by original pool balance.

bullets.title: Cash status
bullets.text: Compare reserve with target and record equity distribution or trapping.

sections.callout: Use exact transaction definitions when the report differs from a simple proxy.

sections.label: Interpret
sections.title: Translate trigger status into cash consequences
sections.kicker: IF THIS, THEN THAT: a failed ratio must change the waterfall.
sections.lead: The point of monitoring is to connect a failed test or deteriorating trend with the next payment-date behavior.

bullets.title: OC fail
bullets.text: Trap spread, pay seniors sequentially and pause residual.

bullets.title: IC fail
bullets.text: May also permit principal for interest; any resulting PDL must be cured.

bullets.title: DQ or CNL breach
bullets.text: Often flips the structure sequential and traps until cure.

bullets.title: Passing tests
bullets.text: May allow equity and pro-rata principal to resume under the documents.

sections.callout: A flag without its cash consequence is incomplete surveillance.

sections.label: Monthly lab
sections.title: Diagnose a failing month and predict the next
sections.kicker: TRIGGER ROOM: calculate the shortfall, then call the cash action.
sections.lead: In month X, interest is $620k, recoveries $25k, fees $97k and note interest $413k, leaving $135k excess spread before principal.

bullets.title: Test result
bullets.text: OC is 1.08x against a 1.10x threshold: fail.

bullets.title: Cash action
bullets.text: Trap the $135k, pay no equity and apply $2.05mm principal sequentially to A first.

bullets.title: Next month
bullets.text: If 60+ falls and OC reaches 1.11x, equity and pro-rata may resume if documents allow.

bullets.title: Decision
bullets.text: Name one trend—such as persistent 90+ delinquency—that would keep equity trapped another month.

sections.callout: Surveillance turns a monthly report into a forward-looking expectation for cash and risk.

flashcards.back: Interest collections divided by senior fees and note interest due.
Reserve target minus beginning reserve; a positive result signals a top-up need.
The monthly record of collections, payments, balances, support and tests.
Principal used for interest that must generally be restored before junior principal.
Ongoing monitoring of collateral, cash flows, protection and trigger status.

quiz.q: What commonly follows an OC fail?
options: Trap spread, turbo seniors, pause equity
quiz.explain: Those actions preserve and rebuild senior protection.

quiz.q: Does every IC fail use principal for interest?
quiz.explain: The legal waterfall governs whether principal can cover interest.

quiz.q: Which bucket best foreshadows near-term charge-offs?
quiz.explain: 90+ is nearest to charge-off.

quiz.q: How do falling recoveries affect OC cure?
quiz.explain: Higher severity consumes spread and delays rebuilding.

quiz.q: What can increase senior extension risk?
quiz.explain: Principal sharing and weak performance can slow senior paydown.

10.title: Capstone: From Presale to Price Talk
10.prerequisite: Days 1–9 · Deal mechanics, performance, surveillance and pricing
10.later: Day 18 · Investor memo and credit pitch

sections.label: Memo
sections.title: Build the one-page investment view
sections.kicker: CAPSTONE START: compress the deal without losing the mechanics.
sections.lead: The memo combines collateral, capital, enhancement, payment rules, tests, operations and agency assumptions in one decision-ready view.

bullets.title: Collateral
bullets.text: Summarize prime or subprime mix, APR, seasoning, LTV and concentrations.

bullets.title: Capital and CE
bullets.text: Show classes, ratings, coupons, WAL, subordination, OC and reserve.

bullets.title: Rules and controls
bullets.text: Capture payment mode, step-up, PDL, tests, accounts and servicing.

bullets.title: Risk logic
bullets.text: Compare agency loss assumptions with available enhancement and mitigants.

sections.callout: A one-pager should explain why the structure deserves its proposed rating and price.

sections.label: Model
sections.title: Run base and stress paths
sections.kicker: TWO FUTURES: same deal, different collateral outcomes.
sections.lead: Model three periods in each path and compare OC, equity, senior principal and a simple WAL proxy.

bullets.title: Base
bullets.text: Use plausible collections and recoveries, keep tests passing and pay residual after reserve target.

bullets.title: Stress
bullets.text: Raise delinquencies, lower recoveries and add $5–10k of fees.

bullets.title: Forced fail
bullets.text: Set OC below target in stress P1, trap spread and turbo seniors.

bullets.title: Cure path
bullets.text: Test whether retained spread and amortization restore OC by P3.

sections.callout: The model must explain equity on/off and the speed of senior deleveraging, not just produce numbers.

sections.label: Price talk
sections.title: Anchor spreads in structure and risk
sections.kicker: MARKET VOICE: state a level and defend it.
sections.lead: Indicative price talk uses WAL, rating, issuer quality, CE and extension features to frame compensation over a benchmark.

bullets.title: Senior guide
bullets.text: The source illustrates T+100–120 bps for a clean 2.5–3.0 year AAA senior.

bullets.title: Mezz guide
bullets.text: The source illustrates T+200–350 bps for 1.5–2.5 year A or BBB risk.

bullets.title: Tighter case
bullets.text: More CE, an earlier sequential flip or a stronger issuer may justify less spread.

bullets.title: Wider case
bullets.text: Long pro-rata, thin spread or weaker collateral may require more compensation.

sections.callout: Price talk is illustrative analysis, not a market quote; explain every adjustment from comparables.

sections.label: Capstone pitch
sections.title: Present Prime Auto 2025-A to the team
sections.kicker: BOSS LEVEL: one memo, two scenarios, one defendable recommendation.
sections.lead: Complete the source exercise by joining a hypothetical deal summary, six modeled paths and concise price talk.

bullets.title: Deliverable 1
bullets.text: Create the one-page memo and a three-period OC table for base and stress.

bullets.title: Deliverable 2
bullets.text: State when equity is on or off and which class receives principal.

bullets.title: Price decision
bullets.text: Propose Class A at T+110 with 3-year WAL and Class B at T+275 with 2-year WAL.

bullets.title: Defence
bullets.text: Give two structural reasons for those levels and name the key downside risk.

sections.callout: A strong pitch links source terms → modeled behavior → investor compensation.

flashcards.back: A concise view of collateral, capital, CE, cash rules, operations, assumptions and risks.
A plausible path with passing tests and ordinary residual distributions.
A weaker path used to test trapping, cure and senior protection.
Indicative yield or spread guidance supported by structure, WAL, issuer and market context.
Senior principal paydown speed used as a simple indicator of average life.

quiz.q: Which feature usually tightens senior spreads?
options: Higher OC and earlier sequential flip
quiz.explain: Stronger protection and faster deleveraging reduce risk.

quiz.q: What happens to equity below OC target?
quiz.explain: Spread is redirected until the test cures.

quiz.q: Quick yield approximation?
quiz.explain: It combines coupon carry and pull-to-par.

quiz.q: Why can long pro-rata extend seniors?
quiz.explain: Less principal reaches seniors while sharing continues.

quiz.q: What is typically first in the waterfall?
quiz.explain: Trustee, servicing and administration costs generally rank first.

11.title: Prime vs Subprime Auto ABS
11.later: Day 16 · Static pools and roll rates

sections.label: Collateral
sections.title: Start with the borrower and vehicle profile
sections.kicker: COMPARE MODE: different collateral creates different deal behavior.
sections.lead: Prime and subprime pools differ in borrower credit, leverage, vehicle mix, term and underwriting controls.

bullets.title: Prime
bullets.text: Generally higher FICO, lower LTV and PTI, newer vehicles and shorter terms.

bullets.title: Subprime
bullets.text: Generally lower or limited credit, higher leverage, older vehicles and longer terms.

bullets.title: Underwriting
bullets.text: Prime is typically tighter; subprime may depend more on dealer networks and verification controls.

bullets.title: Concentration
bullets.text: Dealer and geographic concentrations can matter more when risk is already elevated.

sections.callout: The label is a starting point; pool stratification reveals the actual risk mix.

sections.label: Performance
sections.title: Expect different delinquency and loss shapes
sections.kicker: BEHAVIOR MAP: higher volatility needs more room for error.
sections.lead: Subprime pools usually show higher and more volatile delinquency, net loss and severity, with stronger used-car sensitivity.

bullets.title: Delinquency
bullets.text: Subprime 30, 60 and 90+ levels and roll rates are generally higher.

bullets.title: Loss
bullets.text: Subprime net losses and severity are usually higher and less predictable.

bullets.title: Recovery
bullets.text: Older used vehicles can make subprime recoveries more sensitive to auction prices.

bullets.title: Prepayment
bullets.text: Prime is often faster and steadier; subprime can be slower and cyclical.

sections.callout: Used-car softness can simultaneously raise severity and slow structural rebuilding.

sections.label: Structure
sections.title: Make the structure compensate for collateral risk
sections.kicker: DEFENCE BUILD: thicker cushions and faster senior pay.
sections.lead: Subprime deals commonly use more enhancement, tighter triggers and a stronger sequential bias to protect rated notes.

bullets.title: Thicker CE
bullets.text: More subordination, larger OC targets and bigger reserves.

bullets.title: Earlier triggers
bullets.text: OC, IC, delinquency and CNL conditions can force action sooner.

bullets.title: Sequential bias
bullets.text: Shorter or more conditional pro-rata windows accelerate seniors.

bullets.title: Operations
bullets.text: Cash controls, servicing provisions and PDL mechanics deserve extra attention.

sections.callout: Higher expected loss and rating stress require more available protection.

sections.label: Comparison lab
sections.title: Compare two $100mm capital stacks
sections.kicker: CREDIT MATCHUP: calculate protection, then explain the spread gap.
sections.lead: Use the exercise stacks to compare headline enhancement to Class A and connect the result with expected pricing.

bullets.title: Prime case
bullets.text: A $85mm, B $10mm and OC $3mm: subordination to A is 15%; headline CE is 18% excluding reserve and spread.

bullets.title: Subprime case
bullets.text: A $70mm, B $20mm and OC $7mm: subordination to A is 30%; headline CE is 37% excluding reserve and spread.

bullets.title: Structural decision
bullets.text: List five ways the subprime structure compensates for higher collateral risk.

bullets.title: Pricing decision
bullets.text: Explain why subprime can still trade wider despite its thicker enhancement.

sections.callout: More CE does not make the pools equally risky; it is the structure's response to different loss expectations.

flashcards.back: Generally higher-credit borrowers, lower leverage, newer vehicles and steadier performance.
Generally lower-credit borrowers, higher leverage, older vehicles and more volatile performance.
A stronger tendency to direct principal to seniors rather than share pro-rata.
Visible protection such as subordination, OC and reserve, often stated before excess spread.
Payment-to-income, a measure of required payment relative to borrower income.

quiz.q: Which pool usually has higher 60+ and 90+ delinquency?
quiz.explain: Subprime borrower profiles generally produce higher and more volatile delinquency.

quiz.q: Which is commonly thicker in subprime?
quiz.explain: More structural enhancement compensates for higher expected loss.

quiz.q: Why more sequential bias in subprime?
options: To build protection and reduce senior extension
quiz.explain: Faster senior deleveraging protects against higher losses.

quiz.q: What can falling used-car prices do?
quiz.explain: Lower auction proceeds leave more net loss.

quiz.q: Why can optional advances increase IC risk?
options: Missed interest may not be replaced
quiz.explain: Interest collections can fall short during stress.

12.title: Scenario and Sensitivity Lab
12.prerequisite: Days 5–11 · Performance, modeling, pricing and deal comparison
12.later: Day 18 · Investor memo and credit pitch

sections.label: Drivers
sections.title: Choose variables that move cash and risk
sections.kicker: SCENARIO MENU: stress causes, not just outputs.
sections.lead: A useful scenario changes delinquency, recovery, prepayment and cost assumptions, then observes how the waterfall responds.

bullets.title: Delinquency
bullets.text: Higher 60+ and 90+ can foreshadow more charge-offs.

bullets.title: Severity
bullets.text: Lower recoveries, often from weaker auctions, increase net losses.

bullets.title: Prepayment
bullets.text: Faster or slower principal changes senior paydown and WAL.

bullets.title: Fees
bullets.text: Higher servicing or trustee cost reduces excess spread.

sections.callout: Hold note coupons fixed here so the exercise isolates cash-flow distribution.

sections.label: Paths
sections.title: Build comparable base and stress cases
sections.kicker: CONTROLLED TEST: keep the structure constant and move assumptions.
sections.lead: Run three periods for each case and capture excess spread, reserve, equity, principal and OC on the same template.

bullets.title: Base
bullets.text: Use moderate delinquency, stable recoveries, a full reserve and passing OC and IC.

bullets.title: Stress
bullets.text: Raise 60+ and 90+, lower recoveries, add $5–10k of fees and fail OC in period 1.

bullets.title: Track
bullets.text: Record spread, reserve change, equity, A/B principal and OC each period.

bullets.title: Compare
bullets.text: Explain differences in cure time and senior paydown rather than only listing outputs.

sections.callout: A controlled comparison changes assumptions while preserving the same definitions and model logic.

sections.label: Sensitivity
sections.title: Move one factor at a time
sections.kicker: ISOLATE THE LEVER: severity, prepay or fees.
sections.lead: One-factor sweeps show which assumption drives protection, equity timing, extension and price most strongly.

bullets.title: Severity sweep
bullets.text: Test −5, base, +5 and +10 points and record OC cure time.

bullets.title: Prepay sweep
bullets.text: Move asset principal ±10–20% and observe A paydown speed.

bullets.title: Fee sweep
bullets.text: Add $5k or $10k monthly and measure spread and OC build.

bullets.title: Breakeven
bullets.text: Raise losses until equity remains off for all three periods.

sections.callout: Change one input family at a time so the outcome has a clear explanation.

sections.label: Lab decision
sections.title: Translate model stress into cure and price
sections.kicker: DECISION LAB: when does equity return, and what is the bond impact?
sections.lead: Complete the source exercise with three-period paths, a severity sweep and two simple spread shocks.

bullets.title: Cure test
bullets.text: Report OC and equity on/off for base and stress, plus A principal each period.

bullets.title: Severity decision
bullets.text: Test +0, +5 and +10 points and decide whether equity resumes by period 3.

bullets.title: 25bp shock
bullets.text: At 2.6-year WAL and 99.6 price, estimate ΔP ≈ −2.6 × 0.25% × 99.6, about −0.65 points.

bullets.title: 50bp shock
bullets.text: The same proxy gives about −1.29 points.

sections.callout: Use the WAL price shortcut for intuition only; exact valuation requires projected cash flows and proper duration.

flashcards.back: A coherent set of assumptions describing one possible performance path.
A controlled test that changes one input while holding others constant.
Periods from an OC failure to the first result at or above target.
The loss path at which a defined outcome, such as equity resumption, no longer occurs.
ΔP ≈ −WAL × Δy × Price, a rough intuition tool.

quiz.q: Which two variables most directly raise net losses?
quiz.explain: More defaults and greater severity increase net loss.

quiz.q: What happens below OC target?
quiz.explain: Spread is redirected until protection cures.

quiz.q: Which sweep best isolates extension risk?
quiz.explain: Prepayment changes principal timing most directly.

quiz.q: How do higher fees affect OC build?
quiz.explain: More expense leaves less cash to retain.

quiz.q: What is the rough price proxy?
quiz.explain: Required yield and price move oppositely.

13.title: Legal Documents Deep Dive
13.shortTitle: Find the clauses that control the deal
13.prerequisite: Day 2 · SPV mechanics and true sale; Days 4–12 · Cash rules and tests

sections.label: Document set
sections.title: Know which rulebook answers which question
sections.kicker: DOC MAP: legal form becomes operating behavior.
sections.lead: The indenture, servicing, account and sale agreements divide responsibility for notes, cash, assets and operations; opinions support the intended legal treatment.

bullets.title: Indenture
bullets.text: Notes, covenants, waterfall, defaults, remedies and reporting.

bullets.title: PSA or servicing
bullets.text: Standards, advances, remittance and servicing remedies.

bullets.title: Account agreement
bullets.text: Accounts, investments, control, sweeps and eligible institutions.

bullets.title: Sale agreement
bullets.text: Transfer, eligibility, representations and repurchase for breach.

bullets.title: Opinions
bullets.text: True sale, non-consolidation, perfection and tax conclusions.

sections.callout: Start with the document that legally owns the answer, then use summaries for navigation.

sections.label: Cash rules
sections.title: Find every clause that can redirect cash
sections.kicker: CTRL+F WITH PURPOSE: definitions, waterfall, tests and cures.
sections.lead: Exact definitions and priority language determine whether a ratio passes and who receives the next dollar.

bullets.title: Priority
bullets.text: Read the payment order, principal-for-interest permission and PDL cure.

bullets.title: Tests
bullets.text: Extract OC, IC, delinquency and CNL definitions, thresholds and cure rules.

bullets.title: Reserve and OC
bullets.text: Find targets, floors, step-ups, permitted uses and release conditions.

bullets.title: Calls
bullets.text: Capture coupon step-ups and clean-up call thresholds.

sections.callout: A small definition change in adjusted collateral can change the OC result and equity timing.

sections.label: Control
sections.title: Diligence operational and counterparty protections
sections.kicker: FAILURE MODE: who controls cash when a service provider weakens?
sections.lead: Remittance, eligible-institution and replacement provisions keep collections and critical functions available during counterparty stress.

bullets.title: Cash control
bullets.text: Daily sweeps, blocked accounts and springing lockboxes reduce commingling.

bullets.title: Replacement
bullets.text: Ratings thresholds can force account-bank, trustee or hedge-provider action.

bullets.title: Backup servicing
bullets.text: Check hot or cold status, transition triggers and testing cadence.

bullets.title: Repurchase
bullets.text: Specific eligibility or representation breaches—not ordinary credit loss—typically trigger cure or repurchase.

sections.callout: A springing lockbox at BBB− means cash control tightens when the servicer reaches that downgrade threshold.

sections.label: Diligence lab
sections.title: Build the twelve-point document checklist
sections.kicker: LEGAL QUEST: turn clauses into a repeatable review.
sections.lead: Use the exercise to create a checklist spanning waterfall, protection, operations and asset transfer, then identify the clauses that most affect residual timing.

bullets.title: Cash checklist
bullets.text: Cover waterfall/PDL, OC/IC, reserve, pro-rata and flip conditions.

bullets.title: Operations checklist
bullets.text: Cover advances, remittance/lockbox, investments, downgrade replacement and reporting.

bullets.title: Lifecycle checklist
bullets.text: Cover step-up, clean-up call, swap priority and counterparty terms.

bullets.title: Asset checklist
bullets.text: Cover eligibility, representations, repurchase scope and cure periods.

bullets.title: Decision
bullets.text: Choose two breach clauses and explain exactly how each redirects cash away from equity.

sections.callout: A good checklist records the clause, definition, threshold, consequence and document location.

flashcards.back: The definitive source for notes, covenants, waterfall, defaults, remedies and reporting.
The agreement governing servicing standards, advances, remittance and related remedies.
Legal analysis supporting treatment of the asset transfer as a sale rather than secured borrowing.
Cash control that activates after a defined trigger such as downgrade.
A remedy for specified eligibility or representation defects, not ordinary poor credit performance.

quiz.q: Definitive document for the waterfall?
quiz.explain: The indenture or trust agreement governs exact payment priority.

quiz.q: What does a PDL track?
quiz.explain: It preserves the principal claim for later cure.

quiz.q: Which mitigates commingling?
quiz.explain: Cash moves into controlled accounts sooner.

quiz.q: What usually triggers repurchase?
quiz.explain: Repurchase remedies specific defects rather than normal credit loss.

quiz.q: Where are reserve releases defined?
quiz.explain: Those sections state uses, targets and release conditions.
